images.title: Is twice as tall true
images.purpose: Show that twice Elbrus (5642 m) is 11284 m, which is taller than Everest at 8848 m, so Everest is not twice as tall.
images.composition: Two bars on a baseline with space between, and a dotted grey line above both marking twice the height of the shorter bar.
images.exact_structure: Two vertical bars of equal width on one baseline, drawn to scale with 1 unit = 1000 m. Left bar teal #0072B2 about 5.64 units tall for Elbrus. Right bar amber #E69F00 about 8.85 units tall for Everest. A dotted grey #6B7280 horizontal line across both bars at 11.28 units, which is above the top of the amber bar. A reddish purple #CC79A7 gap between the top of the amber bar and the dotted line. Exactly 2 bars, 1 dotted line.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
bars not drawn to scale, or the dotted line below the top of the Everest bar
images.takeaway: Twice 5642 is 11284, and 8848 is less than that, so Everest is not twice as tall.
images.description: Elbrus 5642 m and Everest 8848 m bars to scale, with a dotted line at 11284 m, twice Elbrus, sitting above the Everest top.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say where twice Elbrus would reach and whether the Everest bar gets there.

image_decisions.why: Checking a claim by computing the doubled value and comparing.
